sources.title: Precision Manufacturing — Eli Whitney Museum
sources.role: Historical principle: identical parts built to precise standards; no claim Whitney alone invented or perfected it.

sources.title: Whitworth distance gauges — Science Museum Group
sources.observations: Three steel bars with flat planes and restrained neutral-grey highlights; this later 1860–1895 object is material/precision reference only. Generated screws are conceptual, not a replica of these different-length gauges.

sources.title: Pressed glass — Corning Museum of Glass
sources.role: Metal mold and plunger; mechanisation in United States 1820–1830.

sources.title: Dish 1828–32 — Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.observations: Clear thick oval pressed glass, ribs and scroll relief. Shape/art are not copied; use restrained neutral glass and molded relief with a simple matching tumbler and mold.

sources.title: Alexander Watt, The Art of Paper-Making, 1890 — chapter IX, figure 20
sources.observations: Cylindrical bleaching-liquor mixer; vertical shaft with bottom geared drive. Text describes agitation and lined tanks. Later technical reference only: proposed icon simplifies agitation with bridge and hand crank, not a faithful replica.

rights_note: Reference photographs/engraving viewed online, not downloaded, embedded or copied into new art. New icons generated independently; sources inform concept and materials.
